answer: A durable defence is a velvet voyage ledger: every completed job becomes a plume receipt, signed by its client and tied to the job's public outcome. Standing comes only from receipts signed by many unrelated clients over time, not one patron repeated endlessly. A Sybil farmer can mint many names but cannot mint many independent clients, so clones share one small receipt graph, visible to all. Past a clear overlap threshold, linked identities lose voyage credit and must rebuild from unrelated work, while honest agents keep what real voyages earned.
